title: Contract Sourcing, Pricing Clauses, and Billing SOP — Contract-to-Revenue Alignment
author: Miguel Santos
body:
Summary:
This document defines the standard operating procedures (SOP) for sourcing customer contracts, standardizing pricing and SLA clauses, and mapping contract events to billing and revenue recognition triggers. It is intended to reduce contract review cycles, ensure consistent accounting treatment, and create clear handoffs between Sales, Legal, Finance, and Procurement.

Scope:
- Applies to all new commercial contracts (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and amendments to existing accounts where contract value >= $10,000 ARR or multi-year commitments are proposed.
- Excludes internal vendor procurement (see procurement SOP) and non-revenue master service agreements (MSAs) under $10k ARR.

Objectives:
1. Standardize clause language for pricing, billing triggers, and SLAs to minimize legal variability and simplify RevRec decisions.
2. Define an approval matrix for discounts, custom payment terms, and data residency addenda.
3. Ensure automated mapping of contract milestones to billing and revenue recognition events.
4. Reduce contract review cycles to <= 5 business days for standard deals.

Definitions:
- Billing Trigger: a contract event that causes Finance to invoice and/or recognize revenue (examples: service activation, delivery milestone, subscription start date).
- Deferred Revenue Event: money received before the service is delivered and recognized under ASC 606.
- Enterprise Commit: a reserved-capacity contract with fixed monthly committed spend.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Sales (Deal Owner): complete Deal Intake Form in Salesforce, select pricing template and expected billing trigger.
- Legal: review non-standard language, insert approved clause variants from Clause Library, sign MSA.
- Finance (Revenue Accounting): confirm RevRec impact, map billing triggers to revenue schedules, advise on contract language.
- Procurement (Customer-side bill-of-materials or HW): handle purchase orders and supplier-side flows.
- Contracts Ops: upload final fully executed contract to Contract Repository and tag metadata.

Approval Matrix (summary):
| Decision | Threshold | Required Approvals | SLA for approval |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Standard pricing & MSA template | Any | Sales + Auto-apply | 2 business days |
| Discount > 20% | > $50k ARR | Sales Manager + Finance Director | 3 business days |
| Custom billing cadence / Net-90 or more | Any | Finance Director + Legal | 5 business days |
| Data residency / On-prem deployment addenda | Any | Legal + InfoSec + Finance | 7 business days |
| Enterprise commit with holdback/penalty language | > $500k total contract value | VP Sales + Head of Finance + Legal | 10 business days |

Contract Clause Standardization (examples):
- Pricing header: "Customer agrees to pay Redwood Inference the fees set forth in Exhibit A. Fees are non-refundable except as stated in Section 5 (Credits & Refunds)."
- Billing Trigger sample snippets: 
  - Subscription: "Billing commences on the Subscription Start Date defined as the date the Service is provisioned to Customer and confirmed by Redwood via email."
  - Enterprise Commit: "Customer will be billed monthly in advance for committed capacity. Usage beyond committed capacity will be billed monthly in arrears at the overage rate set forth in Exhibit A."
- SLA penalty language (template): "If average 30-day availability falls below the SLA threshold (99.5%), Customer is eligible for service credits equal to X% of monthly fees as specified in Exhibit B. Credits are Customer's sole remedy for SLA failures."

Mapping Contract Events to Billing & RevRec (process):
1. At contract signature, Contracts Ops adds metadata fields: contract_value, billing_trigger_type, subscription_start_date, commit_term_months, is_deferred.
2. Finance runs a RevRec pre-check: 
   - If billing is in advance for a future period, flag as deferred revenue and create schedule per ASC 606 (monthly or daily recognition).
   - If billing is milestone-based, link milestone IDs to revenue recognition tasks and estimate percent-complete when applicable.
3. For Enterprise Commits: create a committed revenue schedule and an overage revenue stream; reconcile usage records daily and invoice monthly.

Examples (common scenarios):
- Standard monthly subscription (prepaid): invoice on Subscription Start Date for month 1 in advance -> Recognize revenue ratably across that month.
- Annual prepaid contract: invoice on Start Date for 12 months -> Defer revenue and recognize monthly over 12 months.
- Multi-year Enterprise Commit with ramp: commit fees billed quarterly in advance -> Recognize ratably across quarter, with evidence of performance for ASC 606 satisfied.

Procurement Handshake & PO Flow (when customer issues PO):
1. Sales attaches PO to Deal in Salesforce.
2. Contracts Ops validates PO matches signed MSA/Order Form (customer legal name, billing address, payment terms).
3. If mismatch, Contracts Ops returns issue to Sales with a clear remediation checklist.
4. Once matched, Finance issues invoice per payment terms and logs PO number in ERP for reconciliation.

Contract Variance Checklist (must be confirmed before Legal approval):
- Is pricing template changed? (yes/no)
- Is there non-standard refund or credit language? (yes/no)
- Is there a data residency or encryption change? (yes/no)
- Are there third-party transfer/subprocessor clauses? (yes/no)
- Is there an unusual indemnity or liability cap? (yes/no)
- Does the customer request Net-90 or invoice holdback? (yes/no)

Quick Decisioning Rules (for Sales to self-serve):
- If all answers are "no" on the variance checklist and total ARR < $250k, apply standard e-sign template and route for auto-execution.
- If any "yes" and < $50k ARR, route to Legal Ops for expedited review (48–72 hours).
- If any "yes" and >= $50k ARR, require Legal + Finance manual review.

Clause Library & Templates:
- Location: Contract Repository -> /templates/2026/Standard-MSA-v3.1, Order-Form-Subscription-v2.0, Enterprise-Commit-Addendum-v1.2
- Naming convention: template-type_version_date (example: MSA_v3.1_20260201)
- Maintain a changelog in the template directory and tag releases with the release manager's name.

Operational Playbook (day-of-signature to revenue recognition):
1. Contracts Ops uploads fully executed PDF to repository and populates metadata.
2. System webhook triggers Finance: create billing schedule and set initial invoice.
3. Finance flags RevRec task; revenue accountant confirms recognition schedule and posts deferred revenue journal entries.
4. Billing system sends initial invoice and records receivable.
5. Monthly close: revenue team validates recognition vs usage and posts adjustments before period close.

Automations & Integration Points:
- Salesforce -> Contracts Repository webhook: on contract status = Executed, push PDF + metadata to repository.
- Contracts Repository -> ERP: create contract record with invoicing cadence and PO linkage.
- Usage pipeline -> Billing: daily usage records to compute overage billing for Enterprise commits.

Escalation Paths:
- Time-sensitive commercial negotiations (deadline < 72 hours): Sales flags as "urgent" in Deal Intake Form, Leads from Legal & Finance are paged for triage.
- Accounting disputes: Finance Lead allocates a ticket in the RevRec queue and informs Sales and Customer Success within 24 hours.

Metrics & Targets:
- Contract review cycle time (standard deals): target <= 5 business days.
- Percentage of deals using standard templates: target >= 85% by end of quarter.
- Accuracy of RevRec schedules at initial posting: target >= 98% (measured monthly).

Appendices:
A. Sample Order Form snippet:
```
Exhibit A - Fees
1. Committed Capacity: Customer commits to $50,000 monthly for 12 months.
2. Overage: $0.0025 per token for usage beyond committed capacity.
Billing: Monthly in advance. Subscription Start Date: 2026-03-01.
```
B. Journal entry examples (simplified):
- On invoice for annual prepaid $120,000 on 2026-01-01:
  DR Accounts Receivable 120,000
  CR Deferred Revenue 120,000
  (recognize monthly): DR Deferred Revenue 10,000
                      CR Revenue 10,000

C. Frequently asked questions: short answers to common edge cases (Net-90 requests, tax handling for cross-border customers, reseller flows).
